vista.gap: Frame A renders nothing at all: every one of its 1,440,000 pixels is the same near-black clear colour (RGB 5/8/13, max channel value 13), so there is no terrain, sky, moon, fog, silhouettes, player, or value banding to judge. It is a blank framebuffer, not a vista.
vista.fix: Make the scene actually draw before tuning anything else: set the camera exposure / ambient so the clear colour is not the only thing on screen, and verify the render pass by placing a sky gradient (dark-navy zenith to pale horizon) plus a bright moon disc and a lit ground plane under the player; confirm that a pixel readback shows a real luminance range (horizon near ~180, zenith ~20) before adding fog bands, trees, and ruins back in.
vista.notes: B reads as a coherent, art-directed world because its value structure is deliberate: warm grass foreground, cool faceted cliffs in the mid-ground, and ruins dissolving into pale haze at the horizon, with light shafts tying sky and ground into one tonal system and human figures giving scale.
vista.build: Rebuilt the vista's ground and depth structure: terrain face colours now bake real value variation (olive turf with facet-scale mottling, ragged bare-earth pockets chosen so the overlook stays turf with one dirt pocket in view, straw only on convex moonlit crests, darker worn track with ruts, stronger moon-facing steps and per-face jitter) while grass became three tuft silhouettes in tinted clumps that thin on bare ground and the track, with the worn track re-routed to enter the frame bottom-right as a leading line to the lit Overlook Ruins and a deterministic stone fan plus grass grid filling the camera's near wedge. Depth banding got a quadratic haze curve (four distinct value bands), a notched far crest, stacked-slab crags, and dead-tree lines on the near spur, the ruin ridge and the far cliff band plus trees and boulders strung down the misty valley; moon, fog banding and the single warm brazier accent are kept. Zero console errors; the vista renders ~1.13 M triangles in ~347 draw calls (headless SwiftShader fps 1.7, in its normal 1-3 range).

character.gap: B's hero is hard-faceted flat-shaded blocks with zero tonal gradation or occlusion between parts: the hood is a navy lump, the torso a tan slab, the limbs untapered same-width tubes, and the arm-to-torso and hood-to-shoulder junctions show no darkening, so the body reads as a modeling blockout of primitives rather than a designed character (compounded by the sword blade driving straight into the ground behind the runner).
character.fix: Re-shade the character mesh with weighted/smoothed vertex normals (smoothing angle ~60 degrees on body and limbs, hard edges kept only on cloth hems and the blade) plus a baked or screen-space AO term at the joints, and re-model the limbs with a taper (shoulder/thigh roughly 1.6x the wrist/ankle width) so the silhouette has designed proportions; raise the trailing sword hand so the blade tip clears the ground.
character.notes: A's character has real weight and material unity: the wide-stance windup, the cloth folds and strap detail, the painterly soft shading that matches the mossy rock, and a grounded contact shadow make it read as a deliberately directed hero inside a coherent palette of dark greens, browns, and accent reds.
character.build: Rebuilt the player rig's extremities and run pose so the character reads as a sculpted hero mid-sprint: flat-faceted lofted limbs with calf-bulge shins tapering into cuffed wedge boots (upper + sole slab, heel, pointed toe), bracers that narrow into the wrist, bigger bevelled mitten fists wrapped around the hilt, a jagged tunic hem, slimmer hood, and a narrower darker cloak that lifts with real folds at a sprint. The run cycle now keeps the lean in the spine (pivot pitch halved), drives the far knee with the near leg trailing and its toe skimming the ground, keeps the blade forward-down, and a computed RUN_PH0 lands that hero frame on the pose's 40-step settle; Player now passes a terrain sampler so per-foot contact ovals (plus a faint pelvis oval) are actually placed, and yaw writes straight to the transform. The character pose is reframed right of centre under the moon with pose-only camera side/lift controls so the feet and blade clear both HUD clusters; smoke test 27/27, zero console errors.

combat.gap: The struck enemy in A — the focal point of the whole piece — is an undesigned mid-brown mannequin (plain tunic, grey lump head, no plates/crest/cloth) whose value sits exactly on the mid-brown tent and dirt behind it, and it stands bolt upright with no recoil pose; the spark burst therefore lands on nothing readable and the hit reads as FX sprayed on a capsule rather than a designed foe taking damage.
combat.fix: Re-kit and re-pose the struck enemy: give it a crested kettle helm, one pauldron and a dark charcoal tabard with bone-white trim so its silhouette and value separate from the brown backdrop, pose it in a 3-frame hit-stop recoil (torso bent away from the blade, rear foot sliding with a dust puff), and cast a warm rim light from the spark burst onto its edge so the impact is physically anchored to the body.
combat.notes: B reads as a coherent shipped art direction — unified autumn palette, painterly shading on every surface, each combatant (stick-bundle creature, red-hooded bandit mid-windup, running player) has a unique readable silhouette against value-separated ground — even though it shows the pre-hit beat rather than the impact itself.
combat.build: Found and fixed the real cause of the critic's "pale grey struck enemy": the base Entity hit-flash (white emissive × 0.35) swamped the 7%-albedo soldier regardless of lighting, so Enemy.js now overrides takeHit with a brief weak warm struck tint (blade telegraph heat also cut to a dull red), and the impact point light was cut to 2.4 cd and moved 1.3 m back toward the attacker. The combat pose was rebuilt to be deterministic (no camera lock, since Camera.update keeps blending toward a lock target while posing; explicit orbit + a negative shoulder offset restored by Combat's new afterPose hook) with the soldier planted on the hero's actual blade via boneToWorld/bladePoints, the hero standing 8.5 m from the fire so the camera orbits outside the tent ring, fire and wolf far left, knight right. Arena ground decal widened to 13.5 m with a lifted tan-grey albedo, three-scale breakup, sparse jittered single-boot prints clustered along trodden bands, ash drifts, plus two-tone facet-shaded clutter with extra debris (stones, charcoal, straw, bones); impact sparks reworked into a crisp warm shard burst with motes/chips/ring, dust made earthier and lower, trail body kept faint (a brighter body piled into an additive blob at the hand) with a longer 0.13 s life.

ring.gap: The ring has no vertical volume or spatial boundary: the "wall" is a knee-to-shoulder-high strip of blue flame sprites along the horizon, and above it is plain sky, while the rain streaks are a uniform full-screen particle effect that falls on the player just as heavily as at the ring edge. So there is no threshold, no towering translucent curtain, no cold-tinted interior vs. exterior — it reads as "raining everywhere with a fire hedge", a flat horizon line rather than a weather front closing in. Compounded by a flat grey gradient ground with zero contact shadow under the character and flat black placeholder tree silhouettes.
ring.fix: Replace the global rain emitter with an actual wall mesh: a tall (at least 10x character height, extending above the frame top) vertical ribbon following the ring edge, rendered additive/translucent with a downward-scrolling streak texture, fresnel fade on the side facing the camera, and a depth-fade/soft-particle term at the terrain intersection that drives the existing fire line as the rim glow. Confine the falling streak particles to a ~5m band on either side of that wall so the player stands in dry air facing a curtain, and add a height-fog volume inside the ring tinted 10-15% colder/darker than outside so the interior reads as a different space.
ring.notes: A carries a fully coherent material and lighting language — volumetric blue glow bleeding into wet fog and grass, cool key with warm ember/red accents, layered depth from foreground to the flame wall — so even with the ring relegated to backdrop it reads as a supernatural front, not a strip of sprites.
ring.build: Rewrote src/run/Ring.js so the night ring reads as a weather front instead of a violet dash billboard on a flat plane: the wall is now a dark navy storm body (near-opaque foot, ragged top, luminous cloud cells, subdued rain bunched into curtains) with blue fire at the foot (patch-gated tongues 2-9 m, hot pale-cyan cores that cross the bloom threshold) drawn on the outer shell plus two skirt ribbons for parallax; the world-light hook was retuned (strong dappled flickering contact band, 20 m reach gradient, faint violet fill, colder desaturated grade beyond, so terrain/grass/trees/the player all respond), the ground pool/mist annulus extended inward, the wall light moved to flame height for the player's rim, a near-camera thin-rain streak system and three mote populations (fire sparks, drifting sparkles, gold embers) were added, and the wall's tangent silhouette dissolves when seen from outside the circle. New src/run/Pose.js composes the `ring` pose (player small in the central meadow among dead trees, wall 12 m ahead, low camera, ring held mid-shrink so the HUD shows "THE NIGHT CLOSES IN" and "THE NIGHT DRAWS NEAR"); core/Debug.js only delegates to it (noted in CHANGELOG.md). Capture at /Users/rollins/code/games/nightreign-clone/shots/ring.png, zero console errors.

hud.gap: A's arena floor reads as placeholder geometry: the paving is a scatter of separate, un-joined tile slabs sitting at different heights on a flat grey plane, and under them a fully opaque, hard-edged, saturated gold disc is rendered that neither lights the tiles nor respects them (it shows between the gaps as a flat fill). The disc blows out the night-time value range, flattens the player into a black cutout with no grounding shadow, and makes the whole centre of the frame look like a debug radius gizmo rather than a built arena.
hud.fix: Replace the filled disc with a thin ring decal (2-3% of radius wide, soft-edged, additive, emissive gold) projected onto a single continuous paved floor mesh: merge the tiles into one flush surface with grout-line normal detail and baked AO in the gaps, and add a contact shadow under the player so they sit on the ground instead of floating on a yellow plate.
hud.notes: B's HUD is recessive and exact (bars stepped by stat length, flask count, ornate rune frame, boss bar with name) over gameplay that is unambiguously live: a real leaping boss, a fire damage trail on the player, and a hard cast shadow grounding the character.
hud.build: Rebuilt the HUD to Nightreign's restraint and proportion: thin gradient bars with hot tips over quiet tracks and short cream damage trails (new settleTrails() pose helper replaces the full-width frozen trails), a glowing pale-blue level roundel, a full-width fading top-left panel, plain rune digits with a small dim day/phase line, cool-framed item slots with a fuller sword and painted flask, softer art circles, an 8px boss bar with left-aligned name and sigil, a chest-anchored lock-on reticle, and a Palatino-led serif stack. The hud pose (minimal Debug.js edit) now uses a lower, closer lock-on camera so the player fills the lower centre with the boss towering beyond, and settles both trails before capture. Verified via 1:1 crop comparisons against reference/nightreign/hud/gameplay_2040_08.jpg; smoke test 27/27, zero console errors.

architecture.gap: The church in A is exactly the "boxes" failure the brief warns against: the nave is an intact rectangular block with a flat slab roof, ruler-straight wall tops and three thin floating planks standing in for a "collapse"; the tower is a plain prism with a pyramid cap; there are no buttresses on the side elevations and the walls are a single uniform light-grey value with no base darkening, corner AO, coursing or weathering, so the whole building reads as clean white cardboard propped on the hill rather than a ruin with a history.
architecture.fix: Rebuild the nave as an actual ruin: delete the flat roof slab and leave 3 exposed A-frame rafter pairs (one snapped mid-span, one fallen into the nave), break each nave wall top into a stepped, jagged profile with 3-5 distinct height steps per wall (drop the rear half of one wall to ~40% height so sky shows through the rose-window gable), add 3 stepped trapezoid buttress prisms (~0.8m deep) per side so the side silhouette is no longer a flat plane, scatter 6-10 matching stone-block chunks at the wall base, and apply a vertex-colour gradient (darker/greener at the bottom 1.5m, darkened inside corners) to the stone so the walls stop reading as unlit white paper.
architecture.notes: B's architecture has real relief and layering (recessed arch panels, mouldings, ornament bands, repeated column rhythm) lit with god rays and warm bounce in one harmonious palette, so it reads as a place with history and believable scale at a glance, even though it is a pristine interior colonnade rather than the ruined hilltop church the brief actually asks for.
architecture.build: Finished the orphaned POI.js work by rebuilding the Kit in src/world/Structures.js (frame stack, wedge, fire() with a normal-weighted warm-light bake into vertex colours, seg-subdivided boxes, mottle/damp/mul tinting, stacked-opening gothicWall) and wiring POI.js helpers into it (plus a new lancet() recess and graveyard mix). The church kit was rebuilt for the fixed pose: a 10.5x22 nave with mullioned lancets and buttresses, crow-stepped gable whose right shoulder has fallen to expose the collapsed roof's rafters, gabled porch with a two-order pointed arch and sconces, 17 m west tower with belfry/merlons/pinnacles/spire, lit altar, paved forecourt with stairs and corner braziers, walled and open graveyards, all placed 8 m behind the POI centre so the whole silhouette reads against the fog. The fort gained a gatehouse (twin towers, portcullis, machicolation, torches, banners), corbelled parapets, a taller lit keep and a terrain-measured torch-lit causeway down the hill; the ruin became a roofless abbey with a jagged gable, diminishing arcade, column rows and two braziers. Zero console errors; kits are ~11k/17k/4k tris so the 60 fps budget is unaffected.

bosses.gap: Frame A's composition destroys the boss entirely: the camera is buried against the creature's flank, so roughly 60% of the frame is an undifferentiated grey fur mass with the head, face and most limbs cropped out of view, and the player is fully occluded behind the body. There is no silhouette to read, no scale contrast (nothing to compare the boss against), no visible wind-up telegraph, and the flat overcast midday grassland gives no arena accent or value separation between boss and ground. The name bar is the only thing telling you this is a boss fight.
bosses.fix: Scale the lock-on camera boom by the target's bounding radius for large-bodied bosses (e.g. boom length = max(default, 2.5 x boss radius) with a +10-15 degree pitch bias and a lateral offset toward the player's side), and clamp a minimum camera-to-boss distance so the full profile (head, mane, all four limbs, tail) sits against the sky line with the player visible in the lower-third foreground; additionally drop a rim/key light accent on the boss (warm low sun or a localized volumetric) so its silhouette separates from the mid-value grass.
bosses.notes: Frame B nails the brief's core asks at once: the halberd raised overhead gives a clean telegraph silhouette against the sky, the player in the foreground sells scale, and the cool night blue against warm torch and arena-ring accents reads as a deliberate, coherent palette rather than placeholder geometry (its own weakness is the boss being a uniformly tan, flat-shaded cluster of boxes with no torch-lit rim or rain-wet specular to separate rider from mount).
bosses.build: Built the day-1 field boss as a real class: src/entity/bosses/Sentinel.js is a giant mounted knight on a barded black warhorse (one skeleton, horse + rider bones on the shared RigBuilder/Animator) with its own clips (idle, trot/canter, rearing roar intro, rearing overhead chop with ground-ring telegraph and slam, two sweeps, lance-levelled trample charge, hit/stagger/death) and a gold slot-2 ember material (halberd head, eye slits, visor) that heats on wind-ups; the existing Gravehorn Demon stays as day 2 with its toy-red glow/heat/ring toned down and a fixed pickAttack (Enemy calls it without a distance). Boss.js/Telegraph.js got per-boss glow colour, heat scale and a crisp ring shader; BossArena.js gained cracked flagstone paving, a ruined gate framing the moon, and broken wall stubs; Pose.js recomposes the `boss` pose on the bar (low camera, lock-on style shoulder offset restored by the next snap, Sentinel facing the camera mid wind-up, final ring closed around the arena, pre-aged dust/embers). Wired the roster into Expedition.js (spawnBoss/spawnDebug via createBoss, Nightlord placeholder kept for day 3) and Debug.js (`boss` pose delegates to composeBossPose); smoke test 27/27, headless AI run of both bosses clean, zero console errors.
